messages.subject: survival update
parts:
I've attached an update of the survival routines.
Summary: No change in input or output, some lines removed from mresid2.c.

Long form: I've just released survival2.39 to CRAN, and as part of that update I carefully
worked through several nasty data sets from users, that had given numerical issue in the
likelilhood kernel of coxph. I now understand the issues more thoroughly. In select
cases, certain additions and subtractions need to be done in just the right order so as to
avoid cancellation. The lines removed from mresid2.c guard against a case that, I now
realize, does not happen due to the other changes that had been made.

Terry T.

messages.author: c2082155b3674058
messages.subject: Re: survival update
parts:
Paul,
  The other part of the equation is that all of these edge cases happen due to large values for eta= linear predictor.  (The denominator for all the totals in coxph is sum( exp(eta[i])), summed over those currently at risk.)   I don't think that gbm will ever produce such values.  All the cases I've seen to date involved a very badly skewed but statistically significant variable, so that X \beta was huge for the subject(s) way out in the right hand tail.  I pointed out to the source of the most recent problem data set that they should perhaps question their linearity assumption, since the MLE solution then implied a relative risk of approx 10^40 for one observation, which is greater than the number of atoms in the earth.

The gbm variant does not need to be nearly as "on guard" against these edge cases, it suffices to do things sensibly.

There is one other thing to be aware of, though I don't think it is an issue for gbm.  The first derivative is mX where m is the martingale residual.  Since sum(m) =0, adding a large constant to one of the columns of X leaves the answer unchanged: unless that constant is outrageous.  Adding 10^15 to a 0/1 column would for instance put one at the edge of precision.  So will a term of "x * group" in a coxph model where x is a POSIXct time value and group is 0/1. (Yes I've had such a bug report; it wasn't POSIXct but something very similar in terms of mean vs std).  But again, people don't tend to put interaction terms into a gbm equation.  You shouldn't have to standardize X.

Terry T.
